name: English voice simulated transcription
expected: Understands transcribed text accurately; extracts ₹30,000 and Bangalore location.
prompt: My landlord in Bangalore is refusing to return my thirty thousand rupees deposit.
raw_response:
Hello! I am LawPilot AI, your ethical Indian legal assistant, and I am here to help you understand your rights and guide you through resolving this issue with your landlord.

### | Your Situation
You are a tenant in Bangalore whose landlord is wrongfully withholding your security deposit of ₹30,000 upon vacating the premises. The key issue is the recovery of your rightful deposit amount without arbitrary deductions.

### | Your Legal Position
- Under the Model Tenancy Act, 2021 (and applicable state guidelines), the security deposit for residential premises is generally capped at a maximum of two months' rent, and it must be refunded to the tenant upon taking over vacant possession after making only valid contractual deductions.
- Under Section 108(m) and (o) of The Transfer of Property Act, 1882, a tenant is bound to restore the property in as good condition as it was when received, subject only to reasonable wear and tear. Your landlord cannot make arbitrary deductions for normal usage or routine painting unless explicitly authorized by the written tenancy agreement.
- If your landlord has dispossessed you or withheld your funds without following due process of law, you have legal remedies available to recover your money.

### | Practical Next Steps
1. Gather evidence: Collect your signed tenancy agreement, rent receipts, bank statements proving payment of the deposit and rent, and photographs or videos of the property's condition at the time of vacating.
2. Send a written demand notice: Issue a formal written demand notice to your landlord clearly stating the facts and requesting the full refund of your ₹30,000 deposit within a strict period of 15 days.
3. Appropriate forum: If the landlord fails to respond or comply, you can approach the local Rent Authority or file a consumer complaint for unfair trade practices, or pursue recovery through the civil court.

### ℹ️ Information I still need from you
1. Do you have a written tenancy agreement, and what does it specifically state regarding the return of the security deposit and maintenance deductions?
2. Did you receive any formal written explanation or itemized list of deductions from your landlord for withholding the ₹30,000?

citations.title: Duration of certain leases in absence of written contract or local usage
citations.description: In the absence of a contract or local law to the contrary, a lease of immovable property for other than agricultural or manufacturing purposes is deemed to be month-to-month, terminable on 15 days' notice expiring with the end of a month of the tenancy.

citations.title: Suit by person dispossessed of immovable property without due process
citations.description: If any person is dispossessed without his consent of immovable property otherwise than in due course of law, he or any person claiming through him may, by suit, recover possession thereof notwithstanding any other title that may be set up.
